You are Dato. Build the **Messages / Conversations schema** for InkOS at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`.

## Context

**Why:** InkOS currently has `client_communications` table (channel, direction, status, body, provider_message_id, metadata, timestamps) but NO thread/conversation primitive. TattooClient (the competitor leader) groups all channels (SMS + email + DMs) into per-client threads. InkOS v1 ships with SMS (Twilio) + Email (Resend) — Instagram/FB deferred to v2.

**Plan file Section A2:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/plans/so-we-made-detailed-glistening-frost.md`

**Project CLAUDE.md forbids:** Prisma, Stripe, `any`, tables without RLS.

**Existing:** `client_communications` table. Read the most recent migration for it: `grep -l client_communications supabase/migrations/*.sql`. Match style.

## Build ONE migration: `supabase/migrations/20260421100000_messaging_conversations.sql`

### Table: `conversations`

```
id                  uuid pk default gen_random_uuid()
studio_id           uuid NOT NULL FK → studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
client_id           uuid FK → clients(id) ON DELETE SET NULL   -- nullable until inbound auto-matches
channel             text NOT NULL CHECK (channel in ('sms','email','instagram','facebook','voice'))
external_identifier text NOT NULL                                -- phone E.164 or email address
display_name        text                                          -- caching client name or raw identifier
last_message_at     timestamptz
last_message_preview text                                         -- first 200 chars of last message body for list UI
last_message_direction text CHECK (last_message_direction in ('inbound','outbound'))
assigned_to         uuid FK → auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
unread_count        int NOT NULL default 0                        -- maintained by trigger
archived_at         timestamptz
starred             boolean NOT NULL default false
created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL default now()
updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL default now()

UNIQUE (studio_id, channel, external_identifier)
```

### Alter `client_communications`

```sql
alter table client_communications add column conversation_id uuid references conversations(id) on delete set null;
create index idx_client_comms_conversation_sent on client_communications (conversation_id, sent_at desc nulls last, created_at desc);
```

### Indexes on conversations

- `(studio_id, archived_at nulls first, last_message_at desc nulls last)` — list view w/ non-archived first
- `(studio_id, channel)` — channel filter
- `(client_id)` — client detail
- `(assigned_to, last_message_at desc)` — per-user assigned list

### RLS on conversations

Standard studio-member pattern. 4 policies (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).

### Trigger: `sync_conversation_on_comm_insert`

When a row is inserted into `client_communications` with a `conversation_id`:
- Update the parent conversation's `last_message_at = NEW.sent_at ?? NEW.created_at`
- Update `last_message_preview = left(NEW.body, 200)`
- Update `last_message_direction = NEW.direction`
- If `NEW.direction = 'inbound'`, increment `unread_count`
- Set `updated_at = now()`

### RPC function: `find_or_create_conversation`

```sql
create or replace function find_or_create_conversation(
  p_studio_id uuid,
  p_channel text,
  p_external_identifier text,
  p_client_id uuid default null
) returns uuid language plpgsql security definer as $$
declare
  v_conversation_id uuid;
begin
  select id into v_conversation_id
  from conversations
  where studio_id = p_studio_id
    and channel = p_channel
    and external_identifier = p_external_identifier;

  if v_conversation_id is null then
    insert into conversations (studio_id, channel, external_identifier, client_id)
    values (p_studio_id, p_channel, p_external_identifier, p_client_id)
    returning id into v_conversation_id;
  elsif p_client_id is not null then
    -- Upgrade: attach client_id if we just identified them
    update conversations set client_id = p_client_id, updated_at = now()
    where id = v_conversation_id and client_id is null;
  end if;

  return v_conversation_id;
end;
$$;
```

### Helper: `mark_conversation_read(uuid)` — sets unread_count = 0, updated_at = now(); RLS-safe.

## Types update

Update `lib/supabase/types.ts` with the new `conversations` table + `client_communications.conversation_id` column. Add convenience aliases `Conversation`, `ConversationInsert`, `ConversationUpdate`, `ConversationChannel` union.

## Quality

- Read existing migrations first to match style
- RLS on conversations — all 4 policies
- Every FK indexed
- Trigger must be idempotent (safe on repeat fires)
- `security definer` on the RPC with proper `set search_path = public`
- `pnpm typecheck` clean after types.ts edits

Report: files created/modified, any deviations from spec, typecheck result.

9	## 1. MIGRATION SAFETY
10	
11	### Naming Convention
12	```
13	supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql
14	```
15	Example: `20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql`
16	
17	### Zero-Downtime Migration Rules
18	
19	**SAFE (no lock, no downtime):**
20	```sql
21	-- Add nullable column
22	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN description text;
23	
24	-- Add column with default (Postgres 11+ is instant)
25	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
26	
27	-- Create index concurrently (doesn't lock table)
28	CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
29	
30	-- Create new table
31	CREATE TABLE project_tags (...);
32	
33	-- Add foreign key (NOT VALID skips validation of existing rows)
34	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user
35	  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) NOT VALID;
36	-- Then validate separately (lighter lock):
37	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_user;
38	```
39	
40	**DANGEROUS (locks table, causes downtime):**
41	```sql
42	-- ❌ Adding NOT NULL to existing column without default
43	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN description SET NOT NULL;
44	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Add check constraint
45	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null
46	  CHECK (description IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;
47	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null;
48	
49	-- ❌ Renaming a column (breaks all queries referencing old name)
50	ALTER TABLE projects RENAME COLUMN name TO title;
51	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Expand-migrate-contract pattern
52	-- 1. Add new column: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN title text;
53	-- 2. Backfill: UPDATE projects SET title = name WHERE title IS NULL;
54	-- 3. Switch app code to read/write title
55	-- 4. Drop old: ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN name;
56	
57	-- ❌ Changing column type
58	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN price TYPE numeric;
59	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: New column + backfill + swap
60	
61	-- ❌ CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY
62	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user ON projects(user_id);
63	-- ✅ Always: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
64	```

68	Every migration file should have a corresponding rollback comment:

89	## 2. RLS (Row Level Security) — COMPLETE PATTERNS
90	
91	### Pattern A: User-owned data
92	```sql
93	ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
94	
95	-- Users see only their own projects
96	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own" ON projects
97	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
98	
99	CREATE POLICY "users_insert_own" ON projects
100	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
101	
102	CREATE POLICY "users_update_own" ON projects
103	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id)
104	  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
105	
106	CREATE POLICY "users_delete_own" ON projects
107	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
108	```
109	
110	### Pattern B: Team/org-scoped data
111	```sql
112	-- Members of an org can see org data
113	CREATE POLICY "org_members_select" ON projects
114	  FOR SELECT USING (
115	    org_id IN (
116	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
117	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
118	    )
119	  );
120	
121	-- Only admins can delete
122	CREATE POLICY "org_admins_delete" ON projects
123	  FOR DELETE USING (
124	    org_id IN (
125	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
126	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'admin'
127	    )
128	  );
129	```
130	
131	### Pattern C: Public read, authenticated write
132	```sql
133	CREATE POLICY "anyone_select" ON blog_posts
134	  FOR SELECT USING (published = true);
135	
136	CREATE POLICY "authors_insert" ON blog_posts
137	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = author_id);
138	
139	CREATE POLICY "authors_update" ON blog_posts
140	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = author_id);
141	```

144	```sql

381	## 5. SUPABASE REALTIME SUBSCRIPTIONS
382	
383	### Pattern: Subscribe to table changes (React)
384	```tsx
385	'use client'
386	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
387	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'
388	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
389	
390	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
391	
392	export function useRealtimeProjects(userId: string) {
393	  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([])
394	  const supabase = createClient()
395	
396	  useEffect(() => {
397	    // Initial fetch
398	    supabase
399	      .from('projects')
400	      .select('*')
401	      .eq('user_id', userId)
402	      .then(({ data }) => {
403	        if (data) setProjects(data)
404	      })
405	
406	    // Subscribe to changes
407	    const channel = supabase
408	      .channel('projects-changes')
409	      .on(
410	        'postgres_changes',
411	        {
412	          event: '*',
413	          schema: 'public',
414	          table: 'projects',
415	          filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}`,
416	        },
417	        (payload) => {
418	          if (payload.eventType === 'INSERT') {
419	            setProjects(prev => [...prev, payload.new as Project])
420	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'UPDATE') {
421	            setProjects(prev =>
422	              prev.map(p => p.id === (payload.new as Project).id ? payload.new as Project : p)
423	            )
424	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'DELETE') {
425	            setProjects(prev =>
426	              prev.filter(p => p.id !== (payload.old as Project).id)
427	            )
428	          }
429	        }
430	      )
431	      .subscribe()
432	
433	    // CRITICAL: Cleanup on unmount
434	    return () => {
435	      supabase.removeChannel(channel)
436	    }
437	  }, [userId])
438	
439	  return projects
440	}
441	```
442	
443	### Realtime Rules
444	1. **Always clean up subscriptions** on component unmount (`removeChannel`)
445	2. **Use filters** (`filter: 'user_id=eq.xxx'`) to reduce payload — never subscribe to entire table
446	3. **RLS applies to Realtime** — users only receive changes they're authorized to see
447	4. **Enable Realtime per table** in Supabase Dashboard → Database → Replication
448	5. **Max channels:** ~100 per client connection. Pool carefully.
449	6. **Don't use Realtime for large datasets** — it sends full row payloads. For high-volume, use polling + React Query.

462	- **Edge Functions:** Low-latency global execution, Deno runtime, ~50ms cold start. Use for: lightweight webhooks, image transforms, geolocation-based logic.

526	### Standard Table Template
527	```sql
528	CREATE TABLE public.{table_name} (
529	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
530	  -- ownership
531	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
532	  -- OR for org-scoped:
533	  -- org_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
534	
535	  -- data columns here
536	
537	  -- timestamps (EVERY table gets these)
538	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
539	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
540	);
541	
542	-- RLS (EVERY table)
543	ALTER TABLE public.{table_name} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
544	
545	-- Policies (minimum: SELECT + INSERT for owner)
546	CREATE POLICY "{table}_select" ON public.{table_name}
547	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
548	CREATE POLICY "{table}_insert" ON public.{table_name}
549	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
550	CREATE POLICY "{table}_update" ON public.{table_name}
551	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
552	CREATE POLICY "{table}_delete" ON public.{table_name}

558	-- Auto-update timestamp trigger

615	## 8. BACKUP & DISASTER RECOVERY
616	
617	### Supabase Managed Backups
618	- **Pro plan:** Daily backups, 7-day retention

622	### Manual Backup (before risky migrations)

689	## 10. CONNECTION MANAGEMENT
690	
691	### Supabase Connection Pooling
692	Supabase uses PgBouncer (Supavisor) for connection pooling:
693	- **Port 5432:** Direct connection (limited connections, use for migrations only)
694	- **Port 6543:** Pooled connection (use for application queries)

696	```

698	# For application (pooled)
699	DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres
700	
701	# For migrations (direct)
702	DIRECT_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
703	```

705	### Connection Limits
706	- **Free:** 60 direct + unlimited pooled
707	- **Pro:** 100 direct + unlimited pooled
708	- **Team:** 200 direct + unlimited pooled

714	## 11. DEBUGGING DATABASE ISSUES
715	
716	### Empty Query Results (90% of the time: RLS)
717	```sql
718	-- Check if RLS is blocking
719	SET request.jwt.claims = '{"sub": "user-uuid"}';
720	SET role = 'authenticated';
721	SELECT * FROM projects; -- Does this return rows?
722	RESET role;
723	RESET request.jwt.claims;

726	### Slow Queries
727	```sql
728	-- Find slow queries
729	SELECT query, calls, mean_exec_time, total_exec_time
730	FROM pg_stat_statements
731	ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
732	LIMIT 10;
733	
734	-- Check missing indexes
735	SELECT
736	  relname AS table,
737	  seq_scan, seq_tup_read,
738	  idx_scan, idx_tup_fetch,
739	  CASE WHEN seq_scan > 0
740	    THEN ROUND(seq_tup_read::numeric / seq_scan, 0)
741	    ELSE 0
742	  END AS avg_rows_per_seq_scan
743	FROM pg_stat_user_tables
744	WHERE seq_scan > 100
745	ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC;
746	-- High seq_tup_read + low idx_scan = missing index
747	```

752	SELECT pid, mode, relation::regclass, granted
753	FROM pg_locks

393	-- ── Trigger: auto-increment session_number when booking linked to a project ──
394	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auto_set_session_number()
395	RETURNS TRIGGER
396	LANGUAGE plpgsql
397	AS $$
398	BEGIN
399	  -- Only fire when project_id is newly set and session_number is still null
400	  IF NEW.project_id IS NOT NULL AND NEW.session_number IS NULL THEN
401	    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(session_number), 0) + 1
402	    INTO NEW.session_number
403	    FROM bookings
404	    WHERE project_id = NEW.project_id
405	      AND id != NEW.id;  -- exclude self on UPDATE
406	  END IF;
407	  RETURN NEW;
408	END;
409	$$;

-- ============================================================
-- Migration: 20260421100000_messaging_conversations
-- Purpose  : Messages / Conversations primitive — unified thread
--            model for SMS + Email (Instagram/FB deferred to v2).
--            Groups all client_communications rows under a single
--            conversation per (studio, channel, external_identifier).
-- Tables   : conversations (new)
-- FK adds  : client_communications.conversation_id
-- Triggers : trg_conversations_updated_at
--            trg_sync_conversation_on_comm_insert
-- Functions: find_or_create_conversation(uuid,text,text,uuid)
--            mark_conversation_read(uuid)
-- RLS      : studio_members join pattern — matches projects style
-- Rollback :
--   DROP TRIGGER  IF EXISTS trg_sync_conversation_on_comm_insert ON client_communications;
--   DROP TRIGGER  IF EXISTS trg_conversations_updated_at ON conversations;
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS sync_conversation_on_comm_insert();
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS find_or_create_conversation(uuid,text,text,uuid);
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS mark_conversation_read(uuid);
--   ALTER TABLE  client_communications DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS conversation_id;
--   DROP INDEX   IF EXISTS idx_client_comms_conversation_sent;
--   DROP TABLE   IF EXISTS conversations;
-- ============================================================

-- ── Shared updated_at helper — idempotent (already exists from projects) ──────
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_updated_at()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.updated_at = now();
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- ============================================================
-- 1. conversations
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
  id                      uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

  -- Ownership
  studio_id               uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id)     ON DELETE CASCADE,

  -- The client this thread belongs to; NULL until an inbound message is auto-matched
  client_id               uuid                 REFERENCES clients(id)     ON DELETE SET NULL,

  -- Channel and external address
  channel                 text        NOT NULL
                            CHECK (channel IN ('sms', 'email', 'instagram', 'facebook', 'voice')),
  external_identifier     text        NOT NULL,                            -- E.164 phone or email address

  -- Cached display: client name or raw external_identifier if unmatched
  display_name            text,

  -- Denormalized last-message fields for fast list-view rendering (maintained by trigger)
  last_message_at         timestamptz,
  last_message_preview    text,                                            -- first 200 chars of body
  last_message_direction  text
                            CHECK (last_message_direction IN ('inbound', 'outbound')),

  -- Assignment & inbox state
  assigned_to             uuid                 REFERENCES auth.users(id)  ON DELETE SET NULL,
  unread_count            int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  archived_at             timestamptz,
  starred                 boolean     NOT NULL DEFAULT false,

  -- Timestamps
  created_at              timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at              timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  -- One thread per (studio, channel, address) — prevents duplicate conversation creation
  CONSTRAINT uq_conversations_studio_channel_identifier
    UNIQUE (studio_id, channel, external_identifier)
);

-- ── Indexes on conversations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- Primary list-view: non-archived first, most-recent first
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conversations_studio_list
  ON conversations (studio_id, archived_at NULLS FIRST, last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST);

-- Channel filter (SMS / Email / etc.)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conversations_studio_channel
  ON conversations (studio_id, channel);

-- Client detail — "All conversations with this client"
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conversations_client_id
  ON conversations (client_id);

-- Per-user assigned inbox
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conversations_assigned_to
  ON conversations (assigned_to, last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST);

-- FK support for assigned_to → auth.users
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conversations_assigned_to_fk
  ON conversations (assigned_to);

-- ── updated_at trigger on conversations ──────────────────────────────────────
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_conversations_updated_at ON conversations;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_conversations_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON conversations
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

-- ── RLS on conversations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE conversations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- SELECT: any active studio member can read their studio's conversations
CREATE POLICY "conversations_select"
  ON conversations
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.studio_id      = conversations.studio_id
        AND sm.user_id        = auth.uid()
        AND sm.deactivated_at IS NULL
    )
  );

-- INSERT: owner / admin / artist / receptionist (not guest_artist — they don't send messages)
CREATE POLICY "conversations_insert"
  ON conversations
  FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.studio_id      = conversations.studio_id
        AND sm.user_id        = auth.uid()
        AND sm.deactivated_at IS NULL
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin', 'artist', 'receptionist')
    )
  );

-- UPDATE: owner / admin / artist / receptionist (archive, star, assign, mark-read)
CREATE POLICY "conversations_update"
  ON conversations
  FOR UPDATE
  USING (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.studio_id      = conversations.studio_id
        AND sm.user_id        = auth.uid()
        AND sm.deactivated_at IS NULL
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin', 'artist', 'receptionist')
    )
  );

-- DELETE: owner / admin only (archive is preferred; hard delete is owner/admin only)
CREATE POLICY "conversations_delete"
  ON conversations
  FOR DELETE
  USING (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.studio_id      = conversations.studio_id
        AND sm.user_id        = auth.uid()
        AND sm.deactivated_at IS NULL
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin')
    )
  );

-- ============================================================
-- 2. Alter client_communications — add conversation_id FK
-- ============================================================

ALTER TABLE client_communications
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS conversation_id uuid
    REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

-- Composite index: fetch all messages in a thread, newest first
-- Uses sent_at DESC NULLS LAST so drafts/queued messages don't float to top
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_client_comms_conversation_sent
  ON client_communications (conversation_id, sent_at DESC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC)
  WHERE conversation_id IS NOT NULL;

-- ============================================================
-- 3. Trigger: sync conversation denormalised fields on comm INSERT
-- ============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_conversation_on_comm_insert()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Only fire when a conversation is linked
  IF NEW.conversation_id IS NULL THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  UPDATE conversations
  SET
    last_message_at        = COALESCE(NEW.sent_at, NEW.created_at),
    last_message_preview   = left(NEW.body, 200),
    last_message_direction = NEW.direction,
    -- Increment unread only for inbound messages (staff hasn't seen it yet)
    unread_count           = CASE
                               WHEN NEW.direction = 'inbound'
                               THEN unread_count + 1
                               ELSE unread_count
                             END,
    updated_at             = now()
  WHERE id = NEW.conversation_id;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- Idempotent: drop before recreate so repeated migrations are safe
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_conversation_on_comm_insert ON client_communications;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_conversation_on_comm_insert
  AFTER INSERT ON client_communications
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_conversation_on_comm_insert();

-- ============================================================
-- 4. RPC: find_or_create_conversation
--    Returns the conversation id for (studio, channel, identifier),
--    creating it if it does not yet exist.
--    If it already exists and p_client_id is provided, attaches the
--    client_id when it was previously NULL (inbound auto-match upgrade).
--    SECURITY DEFINER so callers need SELECT on conversations only.
-- ============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION find_or_create_conversation(
  p_studio_id           uuid,
  p_channel             text,
  p_external_identifier text,
  p_client_id           uuid DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS uuid
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_conversation_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Attempt to locate an existing thread
  SELECT id
  INTO   v_conversation_id
  FROM   conversations
  WHERE  studio_id           = p_studio_id
    AND  channel             = p_channel
    AND  external_identifier = p_external_identifier;

  IF v_conversation_id IS NULL THEN
    -- Create new thread
    INSERT INTO conversations (studio_id, channel, external_identifier, client_id)
    VALUES (p_studio_id, p_channel, p_external_identifier, p_client_id)
    RETURNING id INTO v_conversation_id;
  ELSIF p_client_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    -- Upgrade: attach client_id if we just identified who they are
    UPDATE conversations
    SET    client_id  = p_client_id,
           updated_at = now()
    WHERE  id         = v_conversation_id
      AND  client_id IS NULL;
  END IF;

  RETURN v_conversation_id;
END;
$$;

-- ============================================================
-- 5. Helper: mark_conversation_read
--    Sets unread_count = 0 + bumps updated_at for the given
--    conversation.  RLS-safe: callers need UPDATE on conversations,
--    which is enforced by the conversations_update policy above.
-- ============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mark_conversation_read(p_conversation_id uuid)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE conversations
  SET    unread_count = 0,
         updated_at   = now()
  WHERE  id = p_conversation_id;
